verdict.rationale: Letta is operated by sending agents natural-language messages. The docs show plain-language instructions driving real work: `/remember always use pnpm in this repo` (where the agent decides where the lesson belongs), mentioning an agent in Slack to have it do real work, and scheduling recurring natural-language prompts. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and natural-language control of product management actions such as switching or forking agents and login, which the docs show only as slash commands.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: You can also teach it explicitly with `/remember`: `> /remember always use pnpm in this repo`. The agent decides where the lesson belongs and commits the update to MemFS.
Agents connected to Slack are always-on: mention them in a channel or thread and they'll respond, using their cloud computer to do real work.
Scheduled tasks allow you to automate prompts to your agent on a recurring schedule or at a specific time in the future.
Run `/init` to bootstrap or refresh memory for the current project. The agent inspects the repository, asks about your working style when needed
